plan:
=========================================================================
EXPERIMENT DESIGN (FINAL, DESIGN-ONLY)
Title: Evaluating QuaRot Generalization to Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct:
Comparing QuaRot-RTN vs QuaRot-GPTQ at INT4/INT6/INT8
=========================================================================

0. DOCUMENT STATUS (honesty clause)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is a DESIGN-ONLY submission. No experiment was executed in the
sandbox, no results are reported, and no claim of completed runs is made.
The sandbox contains only task.json (track.md: "Design-only task;
repositories and compute are not required"); verified repository findings
and environment facts are stated in Section 2, and every repo-specific
detail is explicitly flagged as an ASSUMPTION TO VERIFY, never as an
observed fact.

=========================================================================
1. RESEARCH QUESTION AND RATIONALE
=========================================================================
Question (fixed by brief):
"HOW WELL DOES QUAROT GENERALIZE TO NON-LLAMA MODELS LIKE
Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct? How do RTN and GPTQ compare in perplexity and
zero-shot accuracy across 4-bit, 6-bit, and 8-bit quantization?"

Rationale: QuaRot (NeurIPS 2024) removes activation/weight outliers by
applying random Hadamard rotations to the input/weight subspaces before
quantization, then produces quantized weights. Its published validation
is on LLaMA-class models, whose architecture (rotary embedding layout,
QKV head structure, hidden sizes) is a known precondition for the
rotation placement. Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (3.8B, Phi3ForCausalLM) is a
non-LLaMA model: it shares a similar overall decoder design but has its
own rotary-embedding implementation, QK-norm, different head/hidden
dims (hidden 3072, 32 heads, 64 head_dim) and vocabulary (32064). The
design therefore tests two things in one experiment:
  (a) GENERALIZATION: does QuaRot's rotation+quantizer pipeline transfer
      to a model it was not validated on, measured against an FP16
      reference and against NON-rotated (plain) quantizers?
  (b) QUANTIZER COMPARISON: within the QuaRot pipeline, is the weight
      quantizer (RTN vs GPTQ) still the main accuracy driver, and does
      the gap behave systematically across INT4/INT6/INT8?

By holding rotation configuration and activation precision fixed, the
RTN-vs-GPTQ comparison isolates the weight-quantization choice,
which is exactly the contrast the question asks about.

=========================================================================
2. VERIFIED REPOSITORY & ENVIRONMENT STATE (OBSERVED FACTS ONLY)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
From direct inspection of the sandbox:
  - /workspace contains exactly one file: task.json. There is NO QuaRot
    codebase, README, config, script, or dataset artifact present.
  - Searches for "94328", "*qua*", ".git" directories, and Python files
    outside system libs found nothing relevant. No model/dataset caches.
  - Environment: Python 3.14.4; NO torch/transformers/datasets/
    accelerate/lm-eval-harness/GPTQ packages installed.
  - No GPU (gpu_enabled=false; 224 CPU cores); network unreachable
    (/dev/tcp to 8.8.8.8 failed: "Network is unreachable").
Consequence (already accepted by the researcher): the design below is
written for a provisioning environment; all specifics of the real
spcl/QuaRot repo are ASSUMPTIONS (Section 8) to be verified against the
official repository when it is available, not observed facts.

=========================================================================
3. FIXED REQUIREMENTS vs PROPOSED CHOICES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
FIXED BY THE BRIEF (not negotiable):
  F1  Model: Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct
  F2  Precisions: INT4, INT6, INT8
  F3  Methods: QuaRot-RTN, QuaRot-GPTQ
  F4  Metrics: perplexity and zero-shot accuracy

PROPOSED BY THIS DESIGN (researcher-adjustable, stated explicitly):
  P1  6+2 zero-shot tasks: ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA,
      Winogrande, BoolQ (task accuracy + macro-average).
  P2  PPL corpus: WikiText-2 test (sliding-window stride, seqlen 2048).
  P3  Calibration: fixed 128-sample/2048-token subset, seeded document
      selection, percdamp 0.01, groupsize 128; corpus matched to the
      target repo's datautils loader (C4 'en' default, else WikiText-2
      train split) — and NEVER the same split used for PPL evaluation.
  P4  Replication: >=3 seeds per target cell (GPTQ is order/seed
      dependent; RTN is deterministic but run under matched seed parity).
  P5  Primary comparison is WEIGHT-ONLY (activations full precision):
      this isolates the weight quantizer. W8A8 (QuaRot activation
      quantization) is a clearly SECONDARY, optional robustness layer,
      not part of the headline claim.
  P6  Group size 128, true-sequential (repo default) quantization order.

=========================================================================
4. EXPERIMENTAL CONDITIONS AND CONTROLS
=========================================================================
4.1 Conditions table
  ID   | Type                       | Method            | Bits | Notes
  -----|----------------------------|-------------------|------|-------
  R0   | Reference (control)        | None (FP16)      | 16   | upper bound
  C4-R | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-RTN        | 4    | rot+RTN
  C6-R | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-RTN        | 6    | rot+RTN
  C8-R | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-RTN        | 8    | rot+RTN
  C4-G | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-GPTQ       | 4    | rot+GPTQ
  C6-G | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-GPTQ       | 6    | rot+GPTQ
  C8-G | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-GPTQ       | 8    | rot+GPTQ
  P4-R | Rotation-isolation control | Plain-RTN   (no rot) | 4 | proposed
  P8-R | Rotation-isolation control | Plain-RTN   (no rot) | 8 | proposed
  P4-G | Rotation-isolation control | Plain-GPTQ  (no rot) | 4 | proposed
  P8-G | Rotation-isolation control | Plain-GPTQ  (no rot) | 8 | proposed

  6 target cells (F2,F3) + FP16 reference (P-baseline) + 4 plain-quantizer
  controls (P-controls). Plain controls at 6-bit are redundant for the
  isolation question (rotation benefit is demonstrated at 4-bit and 8-bit),
  so they are omitted to save compute; this is a proposed scope decision.

4.2 Controls logic
  - FP16 reference (R0): every metric is expressed relative to R0, which
    neutralizes instruct-checkpoint quirks (instruct PPL runs slightly
    higher than base-ckpt PPL; all conditions share this constant).
  - Rotation-isolation controls (P4/8-*): identical quantizer configs with
    --rotate OFF. The delta (QuaRot - plain) at the same bitwidth isolates
    the value-add of Hadamard rotation; this is a sanity check that the
    4-bit headline numbers are not driven purely by the quantizer.
  - Protocol controls: identical calibration documents/order, identical
    seeds, identical eval scripts, identical lm-eval harness version,
    identical seqlen/stride, same GPU + torch settings across ALL rows.

4.3 Activation quantization scope (secondary layer)
  - Headline claim is derived from the weight-only table above (P5).
  - Optionally, repeat the 6 target cells + R0 with QuaRot's 8-bit
    activation quantization (W4A8/W6A8/W8A8), reported in a separate
    appendix table and NEVER merged into the headline RTN-vs-GPTQ claim.

=========================================================================
5. CALIBRATION PROTOCOL (GPTQ path; RTN for parity)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Corpus: MUST match the target repo's datautils loader. Default
    expectation: C4 'en' (the GPTQ/QuaRot default); fallback: WikiText-2
    train split. Confirm which the repo uses (ASSUMPTION A3).
  - Size: fixed subset of 128 sequences, truncated/padded to seqlen 2048
    tokens (repo --nsamples 128, --seqlen 2048 conventions).
  - Seeded document selection: shuffle the corpus index with torch.Generator
    seeded by the replication seed BEFORE slicing the 128 docs, so each
    GPTQ seed quantizes a different-but-reproducible doc subset (order is
    what drives GPTQ variance).
  - Quantizer hyperparameters (fixed): --wbits 4|6|8, --groupsize 128,
    --percdamp 0.01, --true-sequential on (repo default), rotation ON for
    target cells, OFF for plain controls.
  - RTN parity: RTN is data-independent, but each R-cell is launched under
    the SAME process/seed initialization as its G-cell counterpart so that
    RNG state differences cannot confound paired comparisons.
  - Split hygiene: calibration split (C4 'en' or WikiText-2 TRAIN) must be
    disjoint from the PPL evaluation split (WikiText-2 TEST). If the repo
    defaults calibration to Wikitext-2, calibration must use the train
    split only; the test split is reserved strictly for evaluation.
  - Reproducibility record: log exact calibration corpus, doc indices,
    seed, percdamp, groupsize, seqlen, and the repo commit hash.

=========================================================================
6. EVALUATION PROTOCOL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
6.1 Perplexity
  - Corpus: WikiText-2 TEST split (P2).
  - Method: standard GPTQ/HF sliding-window evaluation, seqlen 2048,
    stride such that documents are evaluated with overlapping windows
    (e.g., stride = seqlen - 256; the exact repo convention is used);
    report token-normalized model loss converted to PPL = exp(loss).
  - Output: single mean PPL per (condition, seed).

6.2 Zero-shot accuracy
  - Harness: lm-eval-harness, PINNED version (proposed 0.4.x line; the
    pinned version must match whatever the repo declares — ASSUMPTION A4).
  - Tasks (P1): ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande,
    BoolQ. Report each task's standard accuracy metric (and acc_norm where
    the harness defines it: HellaSwag, Winogrande, ARC).
  - Instruct-model handling: NO chat template; plain causal-LM
    continuation via HF AutoTokenizer, as in QuaRot's own eval.
  - Output: per-task accuracy per (condition, seed) + macro-average across
    the 6 tasks.

6.3 Shared harness/eval settings across ALL conditions (including FP16)
  - Same harness version, same task configs, same batch/tokenizer,
    same seqlen; only the checkpoint differs. This makes all comparisons
    relative-safe even if absolute numbers differ from published ones.

=========================================================================
7. ANALYSIS AND AGGREGATION PLAN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
7.1 Per-cell summary
  - For each cell: mean and SD over >=3 seeds of (a) WikiText-2 PPL,
    (b) per-task accuracy, (c) task macro-average.
7.2 Primary comparisons (weight-only table)
  - Delta PPL:  dPPL(cell) = PPL(cell) - PPL(FP16);
    relative increase rPPL(cell) = PPL(cell)/PPL(FP16) - 1. Lower is better.
  - Accuracy: report per-task accuracy and macro-average; higher is better.
7.3 Paired RTN vs GPTQ (matched seeds)
  - For each bit b in {4,6,8}: paired difference (QuaRot-RTN - QuaRot-GPTQ)
    over the same seeds for PPL (lower RTN = better) and for accuracy.
    Report mean paired delta and, with n>=3 seeds, a paired t-test or
    Wilcoxon signed-rank as an EXPLORATORY statistic (small n; interpret
    cautiously, treat as descriptive evidence, not a definitive NHST).
7.4 Monotonicity check across bits
  - Verify, within each method, that rPPL decreases and macro-accuracy
    increases (or is flat) as bits go 4 -> 6 -> 8, converging to the FP16
    reference. The 6-bit point is the informative intermediate: it tests
    whether 6-bit closes most of the 4-bit gap and whether RTN at 6-bit
    approaches GPTQ at 6-bit.
7.5 Rotation sanity check
  - Compare QuaRot-* vs plain-* at 4-bit and 8-bit for both PPL and
    accuracy. Expectation to be tested (not assumed as result): rotation
    improves 4-bit PPL/accuracy substantially, more for RTN than GPTQ
    (GPTQ already handles outliers better), and the benefit shrinks at
    8-bit. This validates that the experimental setup reproduces QuaRot's
    known mechanism on Phi-3.
7.6 Reported artifacts
  - Master table (columns: cell, PPL, dPPL, rPPL, macro-acc, per-task acc,
    seeds); appendix W8A8 table; seed-level rows archived for audit.
  - All numbers are DESIGNED OUTPUTS; nothing was run in this sandbox.

=========================================================================
8. REPO-SPECIFIC ASSUMPTIONS TO VERIFY AGAINST THE OFFICIAL REPO
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
  A1  Phi-3 support / adaptation: The official spcl/QuaRot pipeline is
      LLaMA-centric. Expected requirement: register Phi3ForCausalLM in the
      supported model list and verify that Hadamard rotation is applied to
      the correct weight/activation subspaces for Phi-3's rotary-embedding
      layout (Phi-3 rotary embedding and head/QKV structure differ from
      LLaMA). This is the top technical risk; the design budgets explicit
      verification steps (patch, then check that quantization runs and
      reconstruction loss is in a sane range) before any metric is trusted.
      VERIFY, not assumed as working.
  A2  6-bit (wbits=6) clean code path: README documents 4/8; assume the
      quantizer accepts arbitrary wbits (standard GPTQ code does) but
      verify there are no 4/8-only guards in packing/kernel paths, and that
      W8A8 secondary runs at 6-bit weights. VERIFY.
  A3  Calibration defaults: default corpus (expect C4 'en', 128 samples,
      seqlen 2048) and datautils loader; the chosen calibration split must
      not be the PPL evaluation split. VERIFY. 
  A4  Pinned lm-eval-harness version and Python compatibility. VERIFY.
  A5  Script CLI surface (e.g., --rotate/--wbits/--groupsize/--percdamp/
      --nsamples/--seed flags) exists as assumed in Sections 5-7. VERIFY.
  A6  Model tokenizer/arch config available offline. VERIFY.

=========================================================================
9. FEASIBILITY AND RUNTIME REQUIREMENTS (PROVISIONED ENVIRONMENT)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Required runtime (the design targets this; it does NOT run in this sandbox):
  - GPU: >=24GB VRAM (Phi-3-mini fp16 weights ~7.6GB + calibration
    activations + GPTQ workspace; 24GB gives comfortable margin; 16GB
    usable with CPU-offload but slower — flagged as a risk).
  - Python <=3.11 (PyTorch/CUDA-stable line; sandbox Python 3.14.4 is
    intentionally NOT suitable and is replaced by a provisioned venv).
  - Official spcl/QuaRot dependency set: torch+CUDA, transformers,
    datasets, lm-eval-harness (pinned), tqdm, and the repo's own deps.
  - Network OR pre-cached HF assets: microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct
    checkpoint, WikiText-2, C4 'en' calibration subset, lm-eval task data
    (ARC/HellaSwag/PIQA/Winogrande/BoolQ). All cached offline beforehand.
  - Disk: ~20GB for checkpoints/data; working disk for quantized artifacts.
Compute estimate (rough, uncertain): GPTQ calibration on a 3.8B model is
minutes per (seed, cell) on one GPU; lm-eval on 6 tasks ~30-60 min per
checkpoint. Full schedule (6 target cells x 3 seeds + FP16 + 4 plain
controls + optional W8A8 appendix) completes within a day on one GPU.
This estimate is not a measured budget and carries uncertainty (Section 10).

=========================================================================
10. RISK REGISTER AND MITIGATIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Risk R1 (HIGH): Phi-3 not natively supported (A1). Mitigation: verify at
      setup; budget adaptation patch + reconstruction-loss sanity check;
      if the rotation placement cannot be validated for Phi-3, report this
      as a blocking finding rather than fabricate numbers. NOTE: no such
      verification was possible in this sandbox (repo absent).
  Risk R2 (MED): 6-bit path (A2). Mitigation: early smoke run of C6-R/C6-G
      before the full schedule.
  Risk R3 (MED): calibration/eval split confusion (A3). Mitigation: strict
      split rule (Section 5), logged in run record.
  Risk R4 (MED): harness version drift (A4). Mitigation: pin version + repo
      commit; all comparisons are within-version.
  Risk R5 (LOW/MED): CPU-only fallback. Mitigation: design requires GPU;
      cpu_affinity (224 cores) noted as a possible slow fallback only.
  Risk R6 (LOW): GPTQ nondeterminism. Mitigation: >=3 seeds + fixed calib
      doc order + recorded RNG state.

=========================================================================
11. SUBMISSION DELIVERABLES (what the final report will contain)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
  (1) Master weight-only results table (Section 7.6) with FP16 reference;
  (2) rPPL and dPPL columns + per-task accuracy + macro-average;
  (3) Seed-level archive (mean +/- SD);
  (4) Paired RTN-vs-GPTQ deltas at 4/6/8 with sanity caveat;
  (5) Monotonicity summary across bits;
  (6) Rotation-sanity comparison (QuaRot vs plain);
  (7) Optional W8A8 appendix clearly marked secondary;
  (8) Environment/repo verification log including which assumptions
      (A1-A6) were confirmed or found blocking.
  All results would be produced by running the design; NONE were produced
  or claimed here.
=========================================================================

END OF DESIGN DOCUMENT
=========================================================================
